channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Shared e-scooters and bikes in Brussels must be returned by September
item.description: The measure applies to free-floating shared scooters and bicycles currently operating in the capital under the cancelled licences.

item.title: Company owned by two MR councillors in Anderlecht under investigation
item.description: Several anti-money laundering experts quoted anonymously said that certain patterns in business operations were allegedly reminiscent of fraud.

item.title: Mural honours Brussels shopkeeper who died after coming to the aid of a woman on a tram
item.description: Driss Atounane, 54, was travelling on Tram 55 in Evere on Thursday afternoon when he intervened in an altercation at the Linde tram stop.

item.title: Brussels roofer seriously injured after falling off scaffolding
item.description: The man fell from a height of about seven to eight metres and suffered severe injuries.

item.title: Brussels for kids: What to do with your family this weekend – 1 to 2 August
item.description: From blowing giant bubbles in a Schaerbeek park, to hitting flowers with a hammer in Forest, we’ve got you covered for summer activities this weekend.

item.title: 'Breathing space': Brussels to get large new park near Midi station
item.description: The new park will transform the Marais Wiels marshes into a fully-fledged park along the train tracks to Brussels-Midi station.

item.title: Who can you trust to look after your pets in Brussels during the holidays?
item.description: While their owners head off on holiday, many of Brussels' pets are preparing for a getaway of their own.

item.title: Licences for shared scooters and bicycles annulled in Brussels
item.description: The high court had been asked to rule on an appeal lodged by the multinational company Lime.

item.title: Over 300,000 Brussels children will receive school allowance benefit
item.description: Iriscare announced on Wednesday that the payment is intended to give every child a good start to the new school year.

item.title: 'They are heroes': Friends knew exactly what to do when they saw a roof on fire in Ixelles
item.description: "Without the swift and decisive intervention of these young men, several people would not have left the scene in time," said a police inspector.

item.title: Molenbeek steps up efforts against drug-related violence following shootings
item.description: The decision was announced following several reported shootings in various local neighbourhoods over the past few days.

item.title: Union Saint-Gilloise star robbed in broad daylight in Brussels
item.description: Striker Mohammed Fuseini was robbed on Sunday while sitting in a parked car in the Belgian capital.

item.title: Brussels shopkeeper dies after defending woman from abuse on tram
item.description: Driss Atounane, 54, died on Sunday morning after falling into a coma following the incident last Thursday.

item.title: Person shot and building firebombed on the same Brussels street
item.description: Two separate investigations were opened into the incidents, which took place hours apart on the same night and on the same Brussels street.

item.title: City of Brussels doubles fines in crackdown on illegal dumping and public urination
item.description: In 2025, the City of Brussels spent €2 million on dealing with waste, including €600,000 to remove 1,891 tonnes of illegally dumped rubbish.

item.title: Actiris opens study space in the Astro Tower in Saint-Josse
item.description: Actiris opens a study space at the Astro Tower in Saint-Josse, Brussels, for young people preparing for resit exams.

item.title: Involuntary manslaughter investigation opened following deadly fire in Schaerbeek
item.description: A Ugandan woman in her forties died in the blaze alongside her 18-year-old daughter, according to unconfirmed reports in Belgian media.

item.title: Brussels firefighters call off strike but warn they will resume if demands aren't met
item.description: The strike, which began on 21 July, was launched over what unions described as structural staff shortages and chronic underfunding at the Fire and Emergency Medical Aid Service (SAIMU).

item.title: Why do we have such a visceral response to the ugliness of Schuman Square?
item.description: The Schuman roundabout was expected to be bold and distinctive, but at some point along the line, someone said, "scratch that".

item.title: Everything you need to know about public transport disruptions in north Brussels this summer ​
item.description: As many people swap Brussels for sunnier climes over the summer, public transport operator STIB-MIVB is carrying out maintenance works.
